test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Feb 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: When was the National Food for Work Programme launched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**14th November 2004**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The National Food for Work Programme** was launched on **14th November 2004**__.
 
• The program was aimed at ensuring food security through employment generation for the rural poor.
 
• It was implemented in 150 of the most backward districts of India.
 
• Under this program, laborers were provided with food grains as part of their wages.
 
• The scheme was subsumed under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) in 2006.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** was enacted on **7th September 2005**__ and came into effect on __**2nd February 2006**__.
 
• MGNREGA aims to enhance the livelihood security of people in rural areas by guaranteeing 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to a rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• The Act provides a legal guarantee for wage employment and also focuses on the sustainability of natural resources.
